lines.text: C.
O.
Her scrubber had *failed.*
The spare cartridges were in locker 7. On my side.
I opened it. Two white cartridges. Exactly like Hale said.
To give her one, I had to open Hatch 3.
Rule one. Never open Hatch 3.
The only rule I had never broken.
I knocked.
Nothing came back.
I said her name out loud. Mara?
Nothing.
Not a knock. Not a scratch.
If the gauge lied about the air, it could lie about anything.
If that room really was vacuum, opening the hatch would kill us both.
Or I would be the one who killed her, by waiting.
Every hatch has a small valve. It lets air through slowly, to match the pressure before you open it.
If there's vacuum on the other side, it roars. And you close it. Fast.
My hand was on that valve for a long time.
I turned it.
A soft hiss.
Then nothing.
The pressure was equal. There was air on the other side.
The gauge had lied. Everyone had lied.
Rule one. Not for anyone. Not even for me.
I spun the wheel anyway.
It was stiff. It hadn't turned in eight months.
Two hundred forty days that door had been closed.
The hatch opened.
It was dark inside.
And she wasn't *moving.*
